frontmatter.title: C4DM Seminar: Understanding the Limitations of Differentiable Reverbs

nodes.html:
C4DM Seminar: Understanding the Limitations of Differentiable Reverbs

QMUL, School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science

Centre for Digital Music Seminar Series

Seminar by: Gloria Dal Santo

Date/time: Wednesday, December 2nd, 2026, 14:00 - 15:00

Location: GC601, Graduate Center, Mile End Campus, Queen Mary University of London

Teams link: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/3137911564917864?p=ULnI4wEN0E0HhnNaBu

Title: Understanding the Limitations of Differentiable Reverbs

Abstract: Differentiable digital signal processing promised us the best of both worlds: the efficiency and interpretability of classic audio algorithms, tuned with the same gradient-based optimizers used to train neural networks. Feedback delay networks (FDNs), a popular structure for efficient artificial reverberation, are a natural candidate. In practice, however, making a differentiable FDN match a real room depends less on the optimizer than on the model. In this talk, I will share what I learned while building optimization pipelines for FDNs, and where they failed. I will argue that much of the difficulty comes from assumptions about the target acoustics, built into the model and the loss, that do not hold in practice, such as a single, homogeneous decay or a noise-free measurement. More broadly, I will discuss which parts of the problem are best handled by an informed design and which are better left to a neural network.

Bio: Gloria Dal Santo is a doctoral student at the Acoustics Lab in the Department of Information and Communications Engineering at Aalto University, Finland. She received her M.Sc. degree in electrical and electronic engineering from EPFL, Switzerland, in 2022. Her research interests include artificial reverberation and the application of machine learning and differentiable digital signal processing to digital audio effects.

C4DM Seminar: Tuning Towards Listening: Decolonize Electronic Music

QMUL, School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science

Centre for Digital Music Seminar Series

Seminar by: Seba Kayan

Date/time: Wednesday, 25th November 2026, 14:00 - 15:00

Location: GC601, Graduate Center, Mile End Campus, Queen Mary University of London

Teams link: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/327412770496677?p=pnhDHpN1CnAPZaKj1Y

Title: Tuning Towards Listening: Decolonize Electronic Music

Abstract: Through the lens of tuning and questions of listening, this lecture explores the cultural assumptions embedded in electronic music and its technologies. Drawing on sound studies, decolonial research and her own artistic practice, Seba Kayan examines how colonial structures and Eurocentric narratives shape listening habits and perceptions of what sounds “in tune.” She approaches instruments and electronic music devices as systems that organise musical attention, asking which relationships they support, what their representations leave out, and how culturally specific ways of hearing can inform their design.

Using examples from her research at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, her productions and collaborative projects such as Hadra Rave, she considers how maqam-led improvisation can guide electronic composition. Maqam-based modal traditions are found in Arabic, Anatolian and Kurdish music, combining characteristic pitch relationships with melodic pathways and practices of improvisation. These traditions include pitches and intonational relationships that are not adequately represented by twelve-tone equal temperament. Listening examples and a practical demonstration make these relationships audible and open up new compositional possibilities. The talk also discusses how mapping pitch estimates onto fixed, equal-tempered note categories can obscure intonation that depends on the maqam, melodic context and performance style.

Approaching listening as a culturally, historically and technologically situated practice, the talk invites participants to question what is treated as musically universal and move beyond the default settings of electronic music production.

Bio: Seba Kayan is a Kurdish-Austrian electronic music composer, producer and lecturer. Her work brings Kurdish, Anatolian and Arabic musical practices into electronic composition, focusing on microtonal tuning, maqam-led improvisation and the politics of listening. She has taught Decolonize Electronic Music at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna. Her work has been presented internationally, including at Ars Electronica, Wiener Festwochen, Biennale Matter of Art (Prague), Visa for Music (Rabat) and the Austrian Cultural Forum (New York). In 2026, she was nominated for an Amadeus Austrian Music Award in the Electronic/Dance category.

Acknowledgement: This talk is supported by the Austrian Cultural Forum London.

frontmatter.title: C4DM PhD student awarded Google PhD Fellowship
frontmatter.author: Admin

nodes.html:
C4DM PhD student Christos Plachouras has been awarded a prestigious Google PhD Fellowship in Machine Perception, in recognition of his pioneering research in audio AI.

The fellowship supports exceptional doctoral students conducting innovative research in computer science and related fields, providing funding and opportunities to engage with leading researchers across academia and industry.

Expanding the Frontiers of Audio AI

Christos Plachouras' research explores how machines can listen to, understand and explain sound using natural language.

Many sectors already rely on automated sound analysis, from biodiversity monitoring in environmental conservation to music recommendation and organisation in the creative industries. However, despite recent advances in artificial intelligence, enabling machines to understand complex audio remains a significant challenge.

Christos' work addresses this challenge by developing improved methods for representing information from sound, generating synthetic training data and evaluating how AI systems interpret audio. His research aims to help create more capable and transparent AI systems that can understand sound beyond human speech. He said:

“I’m delighted to receive the Google PhD Fellowship and excited for the opportunity to advance my research into how machines understand sound. I’m especially grateful to my supervisors and everyone who has supported me for their guidance, encouragement, and trust.”

Recognising the Next Generation of Researchers

Commenting on this year's fellows, Leslie Yeh, Director of Scientific Progress at Google.org, said:

“Every major leap in technology starts with a researcher asking a bold question long before the world sees the answer.

The 2026 Google PhD Fellows are asking those questions today. With funding and a global community behind them, exceptional early-career scientists like Christos Plachouras at Queen Mary University of London have the freedom to pursue ambitious ideas and help build a stronger, more representative scientific landscape for everyone.”

The awards highlight the strength of doctoral research within C4DM and recognise the global impact of research taking place across fields including machine learning and audio intelligence.

You can take a look the complete list of fellowship recipients on Google's website.

The 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR 2026) has just taken place, and we are pleased to announce that the following awards were given to C4DM members:

  • The Best student paper award was given to MAJEPPA: Morphing and Assessing in a Unified Piano Performance Space by Jinwen Zhou, Huan Zhang, Weixi Zhai, Jinhua Liang, Aidan Hogg, Simon Dixon

  • The Best paper award, honorable mention was given to LiveBand: Live Accompaniment Generation in the Audio Domain by Marco Pasini, Javier Nistal, Mathias R. Bjare, Stefan Lattner, George Fazekas

  • Best reviewer awards were given to C4DM PhD students Ben Hayes, Yannis Vasilakis, and Julien Guinot

Congratulations to all! You can explore C4DM's contributions for ISMIR 2026 at: https://c4dm.eecs.qmul.ac.uk/news/2026-11-05.C4DM-at_ISMIR_2026/

The Centre for Digital Music (C4DM) at Queen Mary University of London will be present at the 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR 2026), held 8-12 November 2026 at NYU Abu Dhabi, UAE. The conference theme this year is Crossroads, reflecting the region's position at the intersection of East and West and foregrounding human-centric dimensions of music AI such as social impact, ethics, health and education. The event is hybrid, with both in-person and online participation. C4DM members are involved across the scientific programme, tutorials, and conference organisation.


In the Scientific Programme, the following papers are authored/co-authored by C4DM members:

  • Learning Jazz Pianist Style with Cross-Attention Conditioning (Drew Edwards, Akira Maezawa, Simon Dixon)
  • Steering Dense Music Retrieval With Open-Vocabulary Concept Discovery (Julien Guinot, Alain Riou, Elio Quinton, György Fazekas)
  • LiveBand: Live Accompaniment Generation in the Audio Domain (Marco Pasini, Javier Nistal, Mathias R. Bjare, Stefan Lattner, György Fazekas)
  • MAJEPPA: Morphing and Assessing in a Unified Piano Performance Space (Jinwen Zhou, Huan Zhang, Weixi Zhai, Jinhua Liang, Aidan O. T. Hogg, Simon Dixon)
  • A First Benchmark and Metric for Evaluating Polyphony in Symbolic Music using Voice Independence (Eleanor Row, György Fazekas)
  • Diff2Mix: Controllable Music Mixing via Diffusion Models and Differentiable Audio Effects (Yisu Zong, Jinjie Shi, Joshua Reiss)
  • AudioCodex: Streaming Autoencoders for Live Audio (Marco Pasini, Javier Nistal, Cyran Aouameur, Stefan Lattner, György Fazekas)
  • Equivariant Music Transformer (Zixun Guo, Simon Dixon)
  • Understanding Automatic Mixing: A Subtask-Oriented Analysis of Two-Stage Mixing System (Jinjie Shi, Wei Hua, Kunzhu Xie, Make Li, Yuchen Liu, Joshua Reiss)

C4DM PhD students Yinghao Ma and Weixiong Chen are co-presenting tutorial T4: Evaluating Music Foundation Models: From MIREX To Multimodal, Preference-Aware Benchmarking (with Junyan Jiang and Yizhi Li). The tutorial covers evaluation methodologies for music foundation models, from classical MIREX-style benchmarks through to multimodal and preference-aware approaches.

On the organisational side, C4DM member Christos Plachouras is serving as New to ISMIR Co-Chair for ISMIR 2026.

We look forward to seeing the music information retrieval community in Abu Dhabi and online!
